summary: Markets are displaying a cautiously optimistic but mixed mood, with geopolitical de-escalation between the US and Iran providing relief while persistent uncertainty around Federal Reserve policy keeps investors on edge. The looming Fed decision under Chair Kevin Warsh is a central macro driver, with Kalshi prediction markets closely parsing his likely language around inflation and potential rate paths, while easing West Asia tensions have pushed gold up over 1% and contributed to softer crude oil prices. At the stock level, Apple reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company by surpassing Nvidia, which faces headwinds after news of its potential $250 billion involvement in backing an OpenAI data center lease raised questions about capital allocation and AI trade sustainability, while Boeing and Corning are moving in sharply divergent directions and Coca-Cola's upcoming earnings report will be closely watched as a consumer sentiment barometer. Key risks investors are monitoring include renewed Fed tightening concerns that have already ended a Bitcoin ETF inflow streak, lingering AI sector volatility, geopolitical fragility in West Asia, and potential El Niño-driven climate disruptions with broader economic implications. In the short term, markets are likely to remain choppy and sector-rotational, with tech under selective pressure, industrials and consumer staples attracting dip-buyers, and the Fed decision serving as the pivotal catalyst that will set the directional tone for the days ahead.
